cases.statement: One person: Index case 1, a Portuguese woman (national rare dyslipidaemia study) from a consanguineous couple, homozygous; several myocardial infarctions from age 42.

people.label: Index case 1
people.key_phenotypes: HDL-c below 5 mg/dl (Table 1: 3 mg/dl) and ApoA1 10 mg/dl; premature coronary artery disease with first MI at 42 and repeated MIs; tonsillectomy at age 4; fatty liver disease; normal ophthalmological and neurological exam

quotes.quote: A 48 years-old woman was referred to the genetic department after several myocardial infarctions (MI).
She is the first daughter of a consanguineous couple, and she has a healthy younger brother and two healthy sons.
At that time, the laboratory tests show TC 73 mg/dl, ApoA1 10 mg/dl and HDL-c values lower than 5 mg/dl.
She had tonsillectomy at 4 years of age.
Despite having a normal ophthalmological and neurological exam, severe deficiency of HDL and premature atherosclerotic coronary artery disease suggested Tangier disease.
The genetic study revealed a homozygous variant in ABCA1 gene, c. 3460A>T, p. (Lys1154*) (Figure 1).

phenotype_specificity.statement: Person-level: severe HDL deficiency and premature atherosclerotic CAD led to suspicion of TD. A targeted NGS panel covered the other hypoalphalipoproteinemia genes (APOA1, LCAT, SCARB1); no rare APOA1 or SCARB1 variants were found, and the LCAT variants in the series belong to index case 2 (Table 1). Ophthalmological and neurological exams were normal.

quotes.quote: Despite having a normal ophthalmological and neurological exam, severe deficiency of HDL and premature atherosclerotic coronary artery disease suggested Tangier disease.
Four genes associated to hypoalphalipoproteinemia phenotype were analyzed (ABCA1, APOA1, LCAT and SCARB1).
No rare variants were identified in APOA1 or SCARB1 genes.

segregation.statement: No relatives were tested (cascade screening not carried out). The authors state the sons and parents are obligate carriers. Younger brother and two sons described as healthy (genotypes not tested).

quotes.quote: No relatives were available for cascade screening, but the sons are obligatory heterozygous for the mother’s variant.
Cascade screening was not carried out but, since this patient is a true homozygous patient, her sons and parents are obligatory carriers of this variant.

in_trans.statement: Reported homozygous; parents consanguineous but not tested. The authors call her 'a true homozygous patient'; no parental testing or deletion analysis is reported to confirm homozygosity.

quotes.quote: She is the first daughter of a consanguineous couple
Cascade screening was not carried out but, since this patient is a true homozygous patient, her sons and parents are obligatory carriers of this variant.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense (stop-gain) variant, p.(Lys1154Ter), per the batch HGVS; the paper also calls it a nonsense variant. No statement on ABCA1 disease mechanism (e.g. loss of function) in this paper.

quotes.quote: Patient 1 with a nonsense variant in homozygosity in ABCA1 gene [c.3460A>T, p. (Lys1154*)] presented an unusual phenotype having had several MI around 40 years old.

population_data_in_papers.statement: No frequency is given for this variant. Methods state only that variants with MAF below 5% in gnomAD in the panel genes were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.

quotes.quote: Variants with a minor allele frequency (MAF) below 5% in gnomAD (Karczewski et al., 2019) in one of the genes studied in this work, were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.

authors_classification.statement: Authors classify it as pathogenic under ACMG guidelines; individual criteria are not listed. They state it was not previously described.

quotes.quote: This variant has not been previously described but is classified as pathogenic according to the American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) guidelines (Richards et al., 2015).

concerns: Transcript given only as 'NM_ NM_005502' (no version); batch HGVS is on NM_005502.4.
Age differs: Table 1 gives 42 (apparently age at first MI, matching the lipid values) while the case text says 48 at referral.
HDL differs: Table 1 gives 3 mg/dl, the text 'lower than 5 mg/dl'.
Figure 1 legend describes 'Point symbols' for heterozygous individuals although no relatives were tested; these are presumably obligate carriers, not genotyped.
Homozygosity asserted ('true homozygous') from consanguinity without parental testing.
The paper is a mixed series of 7 dyslipidaemia cases; only index case 1 concerns ABCA1.
notes_for_panel: One homozygous woman from a consanguineous family with severe HDL deficiency and premature CAD; other hypoalphalipoproteinemia genes negative on panel. The authors' ACMG classification is quoted under authors_classification (criteria not listed). No segregation, functional or in-silico data.
